title: The Red Door Persistence

beats.text: Elias ran his thumb over the peeling red paint of the cabin at Mile 14, certain this structure hadn't been on the survey map yesterday morning.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome close up of a hand touching a weathered wooden door in a foggy forest

beats.text: He hiked five miles north toward the ridge to clear his head, but the same grey shingles and rusted latch waited in a completely different clearing.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome wide shot of an isolated small cabin in a dense misty forest

beats.text: A cold sweat broke as Elias whispered the phrase his mentor once warned him about: the door is already unlocked.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome shot of a man's face looking pale and anxious in the shadows

beats.text: He turned and fled toward the valley, pushing through the brush, only to stumble upon the same porch, now smelling faintly of his own childhood home.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome shot of feet running through a foggy forest floor

beats.text: He realized with a hollow dread that the door is already unlocked, and the cabin was not moving; the forest was simply folding into it.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome close up of a rusted door handle turning slowly

beats.text: Inside, his own house keys sat on the kitchen table, and the windows showed only a grey, infinite fog where the rest of the world used to be.
beats.image_prompt: monochrome shot of keys on a dusty wooden table with white fog outside the window

disclosure: An original fictional horror story. Visuals are illustrative.
